_README: Published numbers transcribed by hand from the primary PDFs, for the external
RULE: every value in this file was read off a table in a PDF that was downloaded
and converted with `pdftotext -layout`. Nothing here is recalled from memory or
copied from a secondary source. Each entry names the table it came from so a
reader can check it. Where a paper's own numbers are internally inconsistent
(see `_arithmetic_check`), that is recorded rather than silently corrected.

deepblocker.title: Deep Learning for Blocking in Entity Matching: A Design Space Exploration
deepblocker.authors: Thirumuruganathan, Li, Tang, Ouzzani, Govind, Paulsen, Fung, Doan
deepblocker.recall_definition: Section 5, 'Methods' (p.2466): 'recall is measured as |G intersect C|/|G|, and candidate set size ratio (CSSR) is measured as |C|/|A x B|', where G is the set of true matches between tables A and B. This is pair completeness over the FULL gold set.
deepblocker.candidate_set_definition: Section 5.1 (p.2466): 'K = 10 means that each tuple in Table A is paired with 10 tuples in Table B with the highest cosine scores'. So C = union over a in A of topK(a -> B), and |C| = K * |A|.
deepblocker.serialization: Section 3.1 (p.2461): 'Given two tables A and B, we first convert each tuple into a string by concatenating all of its attribute values.'
deepblocker.vector_pairing: Section 5 setup (p.2466): 'all eight solutions use top-k cosine similarity for the vector pairing module' and 'We used the well-known FAISS library for top-k cosine search'.

table_4_datasets._caption: Table 4: Datasets for our experiments (p.2465). Columns: Table A, Table B, #Matches, #Attr.

table_6_best_dl._caption: Table 6: Comparing with existing state-of-the-art non-DL solutions (p.2469). The 'DL' columns are the best DL method: Autoencoder for structured/dirty, Hybrid for textual. Recall is in percent.
table_6_best_dl._method_note: Neither Autoencoder nor Hybrid is an off-the-shelf sentence encoder: both are trained per dataset on fastText word vectors (Table 3, p.2465). A zero-shot sentence-transformer is a DIFFERENT method, so a gap here is a method gap, not necessarily a harness gap.

uniblocker.title: Towards Universal Dense Blocking for Entity Resolution
uniblocker.authors: Wang, Lin, Han, Chen, Cao, Sun
uniblocker.recall_definition: Section 4.2: 'Pair completeness (also known as recall), is the fraction of true matched pairs identified: PC = |C intersect M|/|M|' and 'Pair quality (also called precision) ... PQ = |C intersect M|/|C|'.
uniblocker.protocol: Section 4.2: 'for cardinality-based methods using k-nearest neighbor (kNN) search, we establish an upper bound on k of 100 as a comparison budget and check the candidates in nearest neighbor order. We evaluate the blockers based on whether they can achieve pair completeness greater than 90%.' Table 3 caption: 'K is the number of nearest neighbors needed to reach the reported PC'.
uniblocker.map_definition: Section 4.2: 'mAP, which is the area under the precision-recall curve (AUC-PR), is calculated as sum_i (R_i - R_{i-1}) P_i where R_i and P_i represent PC and PQ at k = i.'
uniblocker.serialization: Section 5.1: 'In terms of dense blocking baselines, we only serialized record values for effectiveness, using FAISS as the indexer.'
uniblocker.stransformer_identity: INFERENCE (flagged as such, not a quote): Section 5.1 says 'We chose to use the all-mpnet-base-v2 from STransformer [49] as the initial pre-training weight' and Section 5.2 says 'The performance of STransformer, which served as our initialized model for pre-training, is detailed in Table 3.' Together these imply STransformer = sentence-transformers/all-mpnet-base-v2, zero-shot. The paper never writes that identity in one sentence.
uniblocker._arithmetic_check: PQ = PC*|M| / (K*|A|) reproduces the paper's own PQ to 2dp on abt-buy_homo (13*1081; 7.07), amazon-google (13*1363; 6.64), walmart-amazon_homo (27*2554; 1.51), dblp-acm (1*2616; 81.00) and fodors-zagats (2*533; 9.85). This confirms C = union over a in A of topK(a -> B) and |C| = K*|A|, same convention as DeepBlocker. Two rows do NOT reconcile: dblp-scholar (computed 23.77 vs printed 23.38) and, for fodors-zagats, only if |A|=533 rather than the 553 printed in their Table 2 (Fodors has 533 rows) -- i.e. their Table 2 fodors count looks like a typo.

scblock.title: SC-Block: Supervised Contrastive Blocking within Entity Resolution Pipelines
why_not_a_reproduction_target: Section 6.3: recall is measured 'with respect to the test sets of the datasets', i.e. the denominator is only the test-split positives (206 for A-B, 234 for A-G, 193 for W-A per their Table 1), not the full gold set. Every other paper here uses the full gold set.

Their 'SBERT' row is a TRAINED blocker ('Using SBERT's framework we train a supervised nearest neighbour blocker'), not an off-the-shelf sentence encoder, so it is not the zero-shot baseline it looks like.

We could not verify their precision column and do not quote it. Taken as |C & G|/|C| with |C| = k*|A| and a 206-pair test gold, k=5 on A-B would give ~3.8%, but they print 36.2%. A plausible reading (OUR HYPOTHESIS, not their words) is that they restrict the candidate set to pairs that appear in test.csv before computing precision: 206 positives against ~569 retained test pairs would give 36.2%. Either way the definition is not the PQ that DeepBlocker and UniBlocker use, so their precision is not comparable to ours.
